title: Channel partner sell story + technical scoping deck (WIP)
content:
Slide 1 — title
Channel partner sell story + technical scoping (WIP)
Speaker: Aisha Patel (GTM) — rapid field kit for partner-facing technical sellers

Slide 2 — why a partner-focused deck?
- Partners (systems integrators, cloud reseller partners, managed service providers) need a compact narrative that ties business upside to low-friction integration patterns.
- This deck is designed to be a 10–12 slide field kit: sales narrative + 5 minute technical scoping checklist + fallback options.
- Goal: shorten evaluation cycle and give partners repeatable ops playbooks.

Slide 3 — target personas & typical asks
- Partner technical lead: "How quickly can we demo with our infra?"
- Partner solutions architect: "What are min infra/costs, latency, and security constraints?"
- Partner commercial lead: "What are pricing levers and resale margins?"

Slide 4 — one-line value props for partners (scripts)
- For partners reselling managed endpoints: "Redwood gives you consistent SLAs and cost transparency so you can promise predictable performance to your customers without managing model infra."
- For partners offering managed services: "Redwood Private lets you run inference in the customer VPC or on-prem with the dev experience and rollout tooling your ops team expects."

Slide 5 — core technical differentiators (speaker notes)
- Unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private modes (reduces integration branching).
- Smart routing and automatic fallback policies (keep customer apps online during capacity events).
- Built-in prefix/KV caching + batching — real token cost reductions without app logic changes.
- Kernel selection and quantization profiles tuned per workload for predictable latency.

Slide 6 — quick scoping checklist (5 minute)
- Workload type: text generation / chat / embeddings / reranking? (one primary + fallback)
- Concurrency profile: steady vs spiky; typical QPS and burst expectations.
- Latency SLO: p95 target (e.g., <150ms for short-chat, <400ms for long-gen).
- Data residency/security: VPC or on-prem required? KMS/HSM?
- Traffic routing & fallback: single-region or multi-region? Canary policy needed?
- Budget envelope / pricing expectations (cost per 1k tokens or reserved capacity).

Slide 7 — scoping example (SaaS conversational agent)
- Use case: in-app support chat with knowledge base retrieval + short replies.
- Expected QPS: 25 avg, spiking to 250 during product incidents.
- Recommended config: Redwood Dedicated with autoscale burst + KV cache for common prefixes; fallback to smaller quantized model for spikes.
- Estimated monthly tokens: 200M — guidance on reserved capacity vs burst pool.

Slide 8 — common objections + suggested responses
- "We can just run an open-source model ourselves." -> Response: "Yes, but Redwood packages runtime optimizations, routing, and observability that materially reduce ops cost and time-to-launch; we also offer Private for air-gapped cases so you avoid building internal rollout tooling."
- "Latency is more important than cost." -> Response: "We recommend dedicated pools pinned to L models + kernel tuning; we can show p95 benchmarks on similar workloads and a canary plan to validate."
- "We need fine-grained auditability and KMS integration." -> Response: "Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; we have a checklist for SOC/PCI alignment for partner-managed deployments."

Slide 9 — competitor callouts for field sellers
- Compared to hyperscaler managed endpoints: Redwood emphasizes predictable per-token economics and model-version rollouts instead of opaque infra ops.
- Compared to self-hosted runtimes: Redwood provides orchestration, SLO-aware routing, and a developer API that avoids months of engineering effort.

Slide 10 — technical appendix (fast facts to drop into conversations)
- Prefix caching can reduce token cost by 20–60% depending on conversation reuse.
- Continuous batching provides up to 3x throughput improvement in steady-state workloads.
- Dedicated pools offer SLO-backed latency guarantees; typical p95 numbers available per model/seq-length in model catalog.

Slide 11 — integration patterns (diagrams as speaker notes)
- Pattern A: Partner-managed integration (partner calls Redwood hosted API from their service; customer data never stored by partner).
- Pattern B: Customer VPC (Redwood Private control plane + customer-managed inference nodes behind private networking).
- Pattern C: Hybrid (hosted control plane, on-prem inference for sensitive workloads).
- Note: include a short map of auth flows: API key vs mTLS + KMS reference.

Slide 12 — demo checklist for partner POC
- Minimal data set prepared (100–500 example prompts).
- Defined success metric (latency + relevance threshold or F1 for classification).
- Canary rollout plan: 10% traffic -> 50% -> full with automatic fallback.
- Observability hooks: token-level cost dashboard + error traces configured.

Slide 13 — pricing and resale guidance (field script)
- Hosted API: recommend usage-based demo with 30-day credit; show token burn tracking live.
- Dedicated: suggest 3-month reserved pilot with clearly defined QPS targets to estimate commit size.
- Private: license + support; work with engineering to map network/KMS requirements before contract.
- Resale tip: suggest partner margin structures for managed offerings (examples included in appendix).

Slide 14 — partner enablement assets to attach to the pitch
- 30-minute technical deep-dive hands-on workshop script.
- Pre-built Terraform snippets for Dedicated + Private deploys.
- Two sample PRDs: chat support POC, document search POC.
- Quick-start repo link (internal) and contact for solution engineering.

Slide 15 — next steps & owners (action items)
- Field: schedule 1:1 technical deep-dive with partner SA (owner: Marco) — due: +7 days.
- Eng Solutions: prepare a mini benchmark using partner sample prompts (owner: Jessie) — due: +10 days.
- GTM: draft partner commercial template for reseller margin (owner: Aisha) — due: +14 days.

Appendix notes (speaker-only)
- Keep the deck to 10–12 slides for initial pitch; appendices for SAs.
- This deck is intentionally light on vendor names; leave competitor slides as talking points so sellers can tailor.
- Pull live p95/p50 numbers from model-catalog snapshots before each pitch (note: update links in slide footer).

Draft status notes
- This is a WIP — missing: Terraform snippets, sample Terraform module ID, and two demo PRDs.
- Blockers: need up-to-date model catalog latency table (ping eng/metrics), and legal sign-off on reseller margin examples.

Speaker contact

End of deck
